meta.title: Cerebrovascular-Specific Extracellular Matrix Bioink Promotes Blood-Brain Barrier Properties.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A bioink made from decellularized cerebrovascular matrix was coaxially printed with brain endothelial cells into perfusable tubes. The tissue-specific matrix improved blood-brain barrier properties compared with other matrices.

formulations.review_notes: Viability is a threshold ('>95%'). Shell pressure 30 kPa; core 110 kPa.
formulations.name: Cerebrovascular dECM (2.4%) + 0.6% alginate
formulations.composition_detail: 2.4% CBVdECM + 0.6% sodium alginate, core of Pluronic F-127 + CaCl2
formulations.cell_type: human brain microvascular endothelial cells (+ pericytes)
formulations.key_outcome: Cerebrovascular-specific dECM bioink promoted barrier properties; viability stayed >95% over 14 days.

evidence.quote: The final bioink contained 1× Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium, 2.4% CBVdECM, and 0.6% sodium alginate.
at respective temperatures of 4 and 37 °C and respective pneumatic pressures of 30 and 110 kPa
Although all groups showed similar cell viabilities of >95% after 14 d in culture
